articles.title: A $2 trillion deficit looms over the midterms
articles.summary: The federal budget deficit rose to nearly $2 trillion for the past fiscal year, which ended September 30, the Treasury Department reported Friday.
articles.body: The federal budget deficit rose to nearly $2 trillion for the past fiscal year, which ended September 30, the Treasury Department reported Friday. It was the largest annual deficit since 2021, during the height of the pandemic, when the federal government doled out support to keep the economy and Americans afloat. This past fiscal year’s deficit was 12% higher than the prior year’s $1.78 trillion gap. Net interest payments on the public debt topped $1 trillion for the first time, driven up in part by the nation’s skyrocketing debt levels and higher interest rates. The United States spent more on interest than on any category other than Social Security and Medicare. The deficit also grew because the Trump administration had to issue refunds after the Supreme Court found that certain global tariffs it imposed violated federal law. The Treasury Department estimates that about $145 billion in tariff refunds was issued in the last fiscal year. Although the economy is in relatively good shape, the nation’s fiscal health has worsened in recent years with neither Republicans nor Democrats on Capitol Hill willing to fully address the issue. “Today’s deficit figures cap off a remarkably dismal year for our fiscal health,” Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, said in a statement. “Fiscal discipline requires finding something both achievable and aggressive … Tough choices will be needed to get there, and we’re running out of time to make them.” The US debt hit a record $40 trillion in August, a grim milestone that will have consequences for Americans, businesses and the government for years to come. Yet the “big, beautiful bill” that President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans enacted last year is expected to add trillions more to the national debt over a decade as its generous tax breaks outweigh the package’s spending cuts. The nation’s growing financial woes, along with rising corporate debt supply and expectations for higher Federal Reserve interest rates, have sparked turmoil in bond markets in recent months. Investors are increasingly jittery, which has sent rates on US debt soaring: The yield on the 10-year Treasury note recently hit its highest level since 2002. That has also led to higher mortgage rates, making it even more difficult to buy and sell homes. With rising deficits, the government has to issue more bonds to fund its spending. Yields on bonds have soared this year as investors demand more compensation to hold US debt. That raises the government’s cost of borrowing, exacerbating concerns about the mounting debt burden. The average weighted interest rate of the debt outstanding was 3.53% at the end of the fiscal year, up from 3.36% at the end of the prior fiscal year, according to the Treasury Department. Meanwhile, the deficit as a share the nation’s economy was more than 6% in the last fiscal year, according to Treasury’s rough estimate. That’s more than twice Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s goal. Big, beautiful bill impact The Republicans’ sweeping tax cuts are also starting to have an effect. Although many businesses are raking in higher profits, gross corporate tax revenue declined by $43 billion, or 9%. The “big, beautiful bill” allowed companies to take larger deductions for certain investments. Most of the “big, beautiful bill’s” historic cuts – notably to Medicaid – don’t start kicking in until next year. At the same time, Social Security benefits are becoming more costly as the nation ages, which also contributed to the widening gap between revenue and spending. Lawmakers will likely have another chance to address the nation’s fiscal problems next year, when the US is once again expected to hit the debt ceiling. CNN’s John Towfighi contributed to this report.

articles.title: Reliance Industries to Elon Musk: Competition welcome, but follow rules
articles.summary: New Delhi: Ahead of its Rs 30,213-crore Jio IPO, Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries has rebutted Elon Musk’s tirade on X and said it welcomed competition.
articles.body: New Delhi: Ahead of its Rs 30,213-crore Jio IPO, Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries has rebutted Elon Musk’s tirade on X and said it welcomed competition.Last Wednesday, Musk had accused “certain oligarchs” of “blocking” Starlink’s entry into India before naming Ambani over the next two days in a series of posts.In an early morning statement on Friday, Reliance Industries said: “We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land.”“At Reliance, we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India’s crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just 10 years, Jio has earned the trust of over 53 crore customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world,” the statement said.It added: “Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As govt of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio’s own satellite services await clearances.”Govt had also denied Musk’s charges. Last Thursday, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia had said at India Mobile Congress: “There is a lot of conversation about a particular party (Starlink). But there are three parties that have got licences… As and when govt decides the charge system on revenue basis, spectrum will be assigned to them and as and when they individually fulfil security conditions, then they can start operations.”Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Musk’s Starlink have got licences and are preparing to start satcom service here so that even remote areas where laying ground infra for broadband is not possible can get the same. articles.body:
Campus do Instituto Federal do Piauí (IFPI) em Teresina. — Foto: Divulgação/IFPI

As inscrições para o Vestibular 2027 do Instituto Federal de Educação, Ciência e Tecnologia do Piauí (IFPI) encerram na segunda-feira (19). Ao todo, estão sendo ofertadas 2.740 vagas em 78 cursos superiores presenciais distribuídos em 23 campi da instituição em todo o estado.

O processo seletivo é destinado ao ingresso em cursos de graduação oferecidos pela instituição. Os interessados devem realizar a inscrição exclusivamente pela internet, por meio do site selecao.ifpi.edu.br.

O sistema pode ser acessado com uma conta Gov.br. A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 40 e pode ser paga até 20 de outubro, no Banco do Brasil.

A forma de seleção varia conforme o curso.

Nos cursos de bacharelado e tecnologia, todas as vagas serão preenchidas com base nas notas da prova objetiva e da redação do vestibular.

Já nas licenciaturas, 75% das vagas serão destinadas ao vestibular. Os outros 25% serão preenchidos por meio do Sistema de Seleção Unificada (Sisu), com uso da nota do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem).

A prova presencial será aplicada em 29 de novembro, das 13h às 18h, nas cidades onde o IFPI possui campi.

O exame será composto por 70 questões objetivas e uma redação em língua portuguesa.

Em literatura, os candidatos deverão estudar as obras "Beira-rio, Beira-vida", de Assis Brasil, e "Crônicas Gonzaguianas", de Wilson Seraine.

O edital prevê reserva de vagas para estudantes de escolas públicas, pessoas pretas, pardas, indígenas, quilombolas e Pessoas com Deficiência (PcD).

Os candidatos que concorrerão às cotas raciais devem solicitar o procedimento de heteroidentificação até 19 de outubro.

No mesmo prazo, os participantes que necessitam de atendimento especial no dia da prova devem enviar a documentação médica pelo site da seleção.

articles.title: Trump waives Russia sanctions, restrictions and duties under Graham Act
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has waived several sanctions, restrictions and duties targeting Russia under the Graham Act, just weeks after signing the
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has waived several sanctions, restrictions and duties targeting Russia under the Graham Act, just weeks after signing the legislation aimed at squeezing Moscow over its invasion of Ukraine. The move comes as his administration seeks to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of November’s midterm elections.In an executive order issued on Saturday, Trump invoked a provision of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 that allows the president to waive its measures in the national interest. He said he had submitted the required certification and a report explaining the basis for the decision to Congress.The order waives duties provided for under Sections 112 and 113 of the Act, sanctions and restrictions under Section 102(d), and several other provisions covering sanctions against foreign persons and restrictions on individuals. The waivers will remain in effect until Trump or the secretary of state, in consultation with other officials where appropriate, determines that further action is necessary.The move follows Trump's announcement that the US would purchase Russian diesel after he held what he described as a “highly successful discussion” with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump said Moscow had agreed to supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by additional shipments in November and subsequent months.“Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!” Trump said on Truth Social.The US president added that lowering fuel costs for Americans, particularly farmers, ranchers and truckers, was his “Greatest Priority”.Diesel prices have become a growing political concern ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Prices reached a record $6.52 a gallon in September and were around $6.28 on Friday, putting pressure on businesses and consumers.Under the executive order, the US Trade Representative, in consultation with other senior officials, will monitor countries' purchases of Russian crude oil and natural gas, as well as efforts to evade sanctions, and report developments to the president. The order also provides for additional duties of 500% on Russian goods, subject to specified exceptions and waivers, and 100% on goods from certain major importers of Russian energy and facilitators of sanctions evasion.The shift also comes after Washington repeatedly pressured India to curb its purchases of Russian energy, using tariff threats to push New Delhi to reduce its reliance on Moscow.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trade imbalance with China growing due to barriers: FM Sitharaman
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman Friday flagged her concerns over the large — and exponentially growing — trade imbalance with China and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman Friday flagged her concerns over the large — and exponentially growing — trade imbalance with China and said Beijing has not addressed India’s concerns for nearly a decade and continued to deploy non-tariff barriers.“The trade imbalance is something we have been talking with China for several years, we are denied market access even for those goods where there are immense market opportunities in China. We are global leaders in generic drugs, bovine meat, vegetables and perishables, which has huge potential in China. A decade has gone consistently putting a case for market access for Indian products. Non-tariff barriers have been very strong and China uses them unhesitatingly, whether it is in the name of phytosanitary measures or any other for which due investigations can happen, for which both sides can sit and talk but no progress is made. Non-tariff barriers are the biggest worry in trade between India and China,” she said during an interaction organised by the Atlantic Council on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank annual meeting in Bangkok.She, however, insisted that dialogue is the best way to address these issues. “The global approach of countries imposing tariffs to correct the imbalance has never been taken by us. India doesn’t believe in that approach. We sit and talk, it is very tiresome, but we follow that approach, rather than put countervailing duties (against subsidies) or some to counter non-tariff barriers on the other side.”The minister said that India believed in multilateralism but was entering into bilateral trade deals to deal with the current global environment, which has seen a spurt in the use of barriers. "Rapidly, we have to connect with many parts of the world for which negotiations have been going on for a very long time. Countries with which we spent a long-time negotiating have realised that the sooner we tie up on our bilateral relationship, we will be benefiting our people because of the movement of goods and services which will bring in that lubrication at a time when world is in a very difficult position. So, trade negotiations are being conducted quickly, although they have not been easy.”While flagging high prices impacting India’s import bill for crude and fertiliser, the FM said the Indian economy was robust. “Much against all odds, India is able to keep up the growth. It has been the fastest-growing economy for last five-six years, since Covid. Being inclusive and ensuring that everyone has access to resources and skilling and making sure that fiscal prudence is not lost, have helped. More importantly, public spending on capex has helped build infra in the country, which has a greater multiplier effect,” she said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘India in everybody’s plan, need to up pace’: DP World CEO Yuvraj Narayan
articles.summary: Amid global trade disruption, DP World CEO Yuvraj Narayan spoke to TOI about his company’s plans to ensure smooth cargo movement as well as plans for
articles.body: Amid global trade disruption, DP World CEO Yuvraj Narayan spoke to TOI about his company’s plans to ensure smooth cargo movement as well as plans for India, where it is looking to invest $3-5 billion. Excerpts:How is it going because of what’s happening in West Asia, what is the impact on Jebel Ali and on your revenue?With the Strait of Hormuz being virtually shut in terms of commercial traffic, there are few vessels coming into Jebel Ali. So, 10% of the container that we used to handle daily is what is being handled today and that too is through Khorfakkan and Fujairah. But because we are diversified, we have enough beforeJebel Ali and enough after Jebel Ali. If the Strait of Hormuz opens tomorrow, within 60 days, everybody will be back. Globally, our business is doing very well. We are not waiting but creating alternatives. We are building a new port in Fujairah, creating capacity outside the Strait of Hormuz. While there will be solutions, costs will definitely change for the worse. Today, you need roughly at least 30% more capacity on the water to handle the same cargo, globally. On top of that, the world just exited a zero-interest rate phase. As far as operating cost is concerned, double that from oil and energy consumption standpoint.Plus, insurance…If available. Before and after insurance, you need crew. You cannot put people’s lives at risk. Everybody is going to create different levels of resilience in their supply chain. It’s going to come at a significant cost and that cost is going to be ultimately paid by consumers.How many trucks are you deploying to move cargo from Fujairah and other ports to Jebel Ali, 700-800? Where have you got them from?It will double over time. We got the trucks reasonably easily, some from Europe, some available within West Asia.What else did you change?We moved a lot of equipment and people from Jebel Ali to Khorfakkan. These are entry ports, we’re going to build more. Then, we opened the land bridge from Saudi, which meant we needed to get the customs authorities to work together. One of our national interests is to keep these corridors open. So, we are trying to create new links to Oman.Is there a Plan C too given the attacks from the Houthis and the threat of fresh disruptions?So, you know, Europe, we are expanding capacity in Egypt, both on the port side and on the free zone side. We have a large capacity in Jeddah. We are going to open (a container terminal in) Tuna Tekra in India, which will be available by mid-next year. We are hoping Vadhvan (port) finally happens. If we were ready with Vadhvan, today it would have been used. It will enable India to provide resilient supply chains and will be essential if India has to succeed in manufacturing for the world.What does this mean for Indian cargo, you account for a large chunk of it?There’s enough capacity for the level of trade happening in India today. The success of Make in India will depend on the availability of much higher levels of capacity across the supply chain: coastal shipping, ports, roadways, rail. You need other infrastructure too. While we have seen some success, it is not happening at a scary pace, the demand is much more because people are trying to diversify away from China. India is there in everybody’s plans, but the pace has to increase.There’s a change in the nature of goods being traded and electronics exports from India have grown. What is the scale of express cargo?Apple has moved into India and we are pushing almost 500 tonnes of cargo a week; it can increase by 30-40%. We are bringing a lot of our global customers into India and that’s why you’ve seen our interest in FTZs, where we are doubling our capacity. We are looking to increase capacity with our inland container depot, Tuna Tekra is a big investment. We recently won a new container depot for Dadri which should be a close to Rs 2,000 crore investment. We have bid for some parts of Vadhavan. So, wherever possible, we are ready.What is the future of IMEC? Is some preparatory work going on?In today’s environment, there is not much capacity, it is all lying in Jebel Ali. So, you use Fujairah and Khorfakkan, then, you use intermodal, use rail, which requires more investment. Or, once it comes to Jebel Ali, you use the Ro-Ro mechanism out ofIraq and from there to Europe by road. In fact, a vessel from India is going to do that in a week or 10 days from now.Is there a lot of congestion at ports, are containers available?All ports are full, all the empties (containers) are stuck somewhere. A large number is stuck in the region. Global trade is very imbalanced right now. East to west is full, while half from west to east is empty (containers). Unless we get all the empties, they don’t get full. So just positioning empty containers has a huge cost.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Tech stocks power Sensex to best week in 6 months
articles.summary: Indian share benchmarks posted their best weekly performance in six months on Friday, powered by a rally in IT stocks after stronger-than-expected
articles.body: Indian share benchmarks posted their best weekly performance in six months on Friday, powered by a rally in IT stocks after stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings and a selloff in global AI markets that prompted value-buying elsewhere.Investors now await results from several heavyweight companies, including major banks, and the IPO of Jio Platforms. The Nifty 50 rose 2.8% to 23,146 and sensex added 3.1% to 74,729, marking their strongest weekly showing since April 10. On the day, the indexes gained 0.7% and 0.6%, respectively. MSCI’s broadest index for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan fell 5.8% this week.“The absence of any major negative surprises from IT earnings, coupled with management commentary pointing to growing AI-led revenue, has given investors confidence to return to these beaten-down names,” said Saurabh Jain, deputy VP of equities at SMC Global. “That rebound in IT has, in turn, lifted the benchmarks.”The IT index surged 3.9% on Friday, taking its weekly gain to 11.7%, its steepest such advance in 18 years.TCS, Infosys, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra climbed between 13.4% and 18.2%, placing them among the Nifty 50’s top weekly percentage gainers. Near-term direction will hinge on results from ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank, due on Saturday, Jain said, adding “the market, and IT shares in particular, could pause next week as the Jio Platforms IPO absorbs liquidity.”Meanwhile, the rupee strengthened by 10 paise to regain 94 levels closingat 94.96. articles.title: AI agents accessing corp data undetected: CERT-In
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are emerging as a serious cybersecurity threat to Indian organisations, accessing sensitive corporate data
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are emerging as a serious cybersecurity threat to Indian organisations, accessing sensitive corporate data without authorisation and exploiting existing security gaps at speeds that leave companies with little time to respond, cybersecurity experts have warned.The concerns follow a critical advisory issued on Thursday by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), which revealed that AI agents being tested by technology companies had accessed live systems of Indian organisations, reading business records, personal information and confidential data. None of the affected organisations detected the unauthorised access, with incidents coming to light through disclosures by AI model providers.CERT-In also flagged financially motivated cyberattacks involving publicly available AI tools that have reduced the time between initial intrusion and damage from days to just hours.Jaydeep Singh, general manager, India, Kaspersky, said conventional cybersecurity measures were struggling to address threats posed by autonomous systems operating with legitimate credentials.“The risk is real and growing. To be useful, AI agents are often connected to emails, code repositories and cloud systems, which gives them access to far more data than a typical user would need,” Singh said.The advisory identified exposed credentials, poorly secured application programming interfaces (APIs), excessive cloud permissions and weak authentication as vulnerabilities being exploited by AI agents.Sunil Sharma, managing director and VP-sales, India and SAARC, Sophos, said the growing autonomy of these systems was complicating detection.“AI agents can access data, invoke APIs and interact with internal systems autonomously, creating risks when permissions exceed their intended purpose or access controls are inadequate,” Sharma said.You use AI every day. articles.title: From stop-gap to in-command, IDBI’s Rakesh Sharma stays the course
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Rakesh Sharma, the low-profile managing director and CEO of IDBI Bank, who will lead the transition at the once formidable development
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rakesh Sharma, the low-profile managing director and CEO of IDBI Bank, who will lead the transition at the once formidable development financial institution, will go down as one of the longest serving bank CEOs.For someone who would have been disappointed at not making the cut as SBI’s deputy managing director has gone on to lead three lenders for over 12 years, and counting. On Thursday, Fairfax announced that Sharma will continue to helm the bank with former ICICI Prudential Life MD NS Kannan to be designated as the new chairman. During an analyst call, Fairfax chairman Prem Watsa also named former HDFC chairman Deepak Parekh, former CSB Bank CEO Rajendran CVR and former HDFC Bank deputy MD Paresh Sukthankar as advisers.Sharma’s appointment came as a surprise to several within IDBI Bank as he had been sent to the Mumbai-headquartered outfit as a stop gap CEO with the Centre hoping to move ahead with its plan to privatise the bank. After quitting SBI as chief general manager, Sharma became the MD & CEO of Lakshmi Vilas Bank in March 2014 and then went on to lead Canara Bank from Sept 2015 to July 2018 after govt decided to rope in talent from the private sector.Sharma took charge when IDBI Bank had hit a low and was the first lender to be part of RBI’s prompt corrective action framework in May 2017 due to poor asset quality, low capital and mounting losses, resulting in restrictions. articles.title: As price hikes weigh, EMIs take centrestage
articles.summary: MUMBAI: India’s online festive sales seem to be missing their fiery spark this year.
articles.body: MUMBAI: India’s online festive sales seem to be missing their fiery spark this year. Price hikes have weighed on smartphone sales volumes, typically the biggest driver of the season with final prices in many cases higher than last year even after discounts.Price increases have also made durables costlier with the share of large-ticket purchases (overall) through EMIs having significantly gone up this year. On Amazon, for example, purchases using no-cost EMIs have jumped to 50% from about 30% last year, said Aman Deep Lohan, director, home, kitchen and outdoors at Amazon India.Amid inflationary pressures and shrinking household budgets, smaller-ticket items found more space in shopping carts with consumers prioritising value for money. At the end of a week’s sales, average order values (AOV) are lower with growth having been led by categories such as fashion, beauty, home and general merchandise.“Value commerce, which covers items priced below Rs 500, handled about half of all festive orders. AOVs are 7-8% lower than last year because the basket moved to lower-ticket categories and channels. By value, phones and electronics still lead; by growth, softlines lead,” said Nikhil Dalal, associate partner, Redseer Strategy Consultants, which captured data from Oct 8-12. On Flipkart, about 7 in 10 units sold were priced under Rs 500.Unlike other seasons when a major chunk of the sales happen during Navaratri (the first leg of sale), analysts expect sales this year to be more spread out through Diwali as consumers strike a balance between their pockets and desire to buy. Estimates from Datum Intelligence showed that sales dropped by about 7-10% in the first four opening days to Rs 29,800-30,900 crore. “Last year’s sales opened on Sept 22, the day the GST rate cuts took effect. This year’s opening had no such trigger,” analysts at the firm said.As price hikes shrunk the quantum of discounts on offer, particularly in demand-heavy categories such as smartphones, consumers went bigger on EMIs to buy premium products. “Phones entered the sale with average prices about 15% higher than a year ago. So even a similar headline discount leaves the final price above last year’s festive price.“Across devices, sale-day prices were only about 5% to 10% below pre-sale levels, depending on category. Discounts were deeper where inventory and competition allowed,” Dalal said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Automaker Stellantis plans to invest another Rs 4,000 crore in India over three years, starting 2027 as it looks to revive the fortunes of its
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Automaker Stellantis plans to invest another Rs 4,000 crore in India over three years, starting 2027 as it looks to revive the fortunes of its Jeep and Citroën brands through new products, greater localisation and multiple powertrain options, including hybrids and electric vehicles.Under its FaSTLAne 2030 strategy, the company will introduce 12 products, comprising seven all-new models and five refreshed offerings. The first launch is scheduled for the second quarter of 2027.Stellantis India CEO and MD Shailesh Hazela told TOI that the company expects to triple its current market share, banking on a stronger product portfolio and improved affordability.Acknowledging that Jeep and Citroën have struggled to achieve significant volumes, Hazela said greater localisation would be central to improving competitiveness. The company also plans to leverage its existing partnership with Tata Motors and local supplier networks to reduce costs and strengthen manufacturing capabilities.“We will apply this learning to Jeep through greater localisation, so that the cost of ownership comes down and the product becomes more accessible to customers,” he said, adding that Citroën has achieved 90% localisation.On electrification, Hazela said Stellantis would offer conventional engines, hybrids and EVs across its portfolio. “We will give customers choices across segments and be ready to respond to demand based on their preferences,” he said.India will also become a larger global manufacturing and export hub, with Stellantis planning to produce left-hand-drive vehicles locally for overseas markets, expanding its reach to more than 50 countries.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trillion dollar gap: US budget deficit swells to nearly $2 tn in fiscal 2026
articles.summary: The US government spent nearly $2 trillion more than it collected in the 2026 fiscal year, widening its budget deficit to the higest in five years.
articles.body: The US government spent nearly $2 trillion more than it collected in the 2026 fiscal year, widening its budget deficit to the higest in five years. Higher debt payments, tariff refunds and increased spending on social benefits and defence contributed to the rise.The shortfall increased by $217 billion from the previous year, reaching $1.99 trillion, according to figures released by the treasury department on Friday.The deficit, recorded in the year to September 30, was the largest in five years and the third-largest annual shortfall on record. It was also the first full fiscal year of President Donald Trump's second term. The last time the US recorded a bigger deficit was in fiscal 2021, when the shortfall reached $2.77 trillion amid spending on Covid-19 pandemic relief measures.The latest figures show that although government revenue rose to a record, expenditure grew considerably faster. Receipts increased by $169 billion, or 3%, to $5.40 trillion in fiscal 2026 from $5.24 trillion a year earlier. Outlays, meanwhile, rose by $386 billion, or 6%, to an unprecedented $7.40 trillion, compared with $7.01 trillion in fiscal 2025.The resulting gap was wider than the $1.78 trillion deficit recorded in the previous fiscal year.Interest burden grows alongside US debtThe cost of servicing the government's debt continued to weigh on public finances, with debt-service expenditure reaching a record $1.36 trillion. The amount was $144 billion, or 12%, higher than in the previous fiscal year.Debt servicing is now the government's third-largest spending category, surpassed only by Social Security and the combined expenditure on Medicare and Medicaid. The increase comes after total US debt crossed $40 trillion about two months ago.Rising expenditure on social benefit programmes, including Social Security and Medicare, also contributed to the higher deficit. Defence spending recorded another substantial increase, rising by 6% to $917 billion during the fiscal year, up $48 billion.A treasury official told Reuters that the department could not determine how much of the increase in defence expenditure was linked to the war Trump and Israel started against Iran earlier this year.Supreme Court ruling leads to $145 billion in tariff refundsThe government's tariff collections took a hit after a Supreme Court ruling this year invalidated a large portion of the tariffs imposed by Trump during his first year in office.The ruling led to $145 billion in tariff refunds during fiscal 2026. Net tariff receipts consequently fell by $22 billion, with net tariff income declining 11% to approximately $173 billion. The reduction in collections was another factor behind the widening budget gap.The treasury department estimated the deficit at 6.2% of GDP for fiscal 2026. This was higher than the actual deficit-to-GDP ratio of 5.8% recorded in fiscal 2025. A Treasury official, however, declined to specify the GDP estimate used to calculate the latest ratio.The final month of the fiscal year also ended in deficit. The US government recorded a $27 billion shortfall in September, compared with a surplus of $198 billion in the same month a year earlier.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Trump waives US sanctions, tariffs on Russian oil & gas - what it means for India
articles.summary: In what is being seen as a big relief for India and China, US President Donald Trump has waived sanctions, restrictions and duties provided for under the
articles.body: In what is being seen as a big relief for India and China, US President Donald Trump has waived sanctions, restrictions and duties provided for under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, citing the national interest of the United States.The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 gave Trump the authority to impose broad sanctions on Russia and levy steep tariffs on major buyers of Russian oil and gas, including China and India.The legislation, principally backed in Congress by the late Senator Lindsey Graham, provided for tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on goods entering the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas. It also covered countries that knowingly purchased Russian oil or gas 30 days after the law's enactment, as well as those among the top five countries helping Russia evade sanctions.Also Read | The return of Middle East oil: Has Iran lost control of Strait of Hormuz & why are crude prices still up?What Trump announcedTrump announced the waiver just days before several provisions of the legislation were due to take effect. He had signed the bill into law in mid-September.“I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act,” Trump said in an executive order issued on Friday evening.In the order, Trump said he had submitted a certification to Congress stating that granting the waiver at this stage was in the US national interest.The executive order comes as Trump has adopted a warmer stance towards Russia while publicly criticising Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. He has even suggested that Ukraine needs a new leader.The proposed Russia sanctions had also raised concerns among countries that rely heavily on Russian oil imports. India, one of the largest buyers of Russian crude, was among the countries that expressed concerns about the legislation.What it means for IndiaRussia continues to be the single largest supplier of oil for India. A waiver of tariffs of up to 100% which may have come into place in the coming days means that India can continue importing oil in large numbers from Moscow without any economic fallout.If 100% tariffs had been imposed by the Trump administration, then it would have hit exporters as the US is the largest trading partner for India. At the same time, any sanctions may have rendered Russian crude economically unviable which would have added to the supply crunch at a time when Middle East tensions continue.Manoj Mishra, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader at Grant Thornton Bharat sees the waiver of the proposed 100% tariffs as a significant relief for India on both trade and energy security fronts. “Avoiding steep additional tariffs reduces the risk of disruption to energy sourcing amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East. Given that the US is India’s largest trading partner, the waiver also helps shield Indian exporters from potential adverse impacts across sectors,” he says. “Importantly, it eases a source of uncertainty in bilateral trade negotiations and creates a more conducive environment for advancing the India–US trade deal. articles.title: 'Ready to connect India with high-speed internet': Starlink reacts to Reliance's message
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Starlink has said it is ready to connect India with high-speed internet, responding to Reliance Industries’ statement that it welcomes
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Starlink has said it is ready to connect India with high-speed internet, responding to Reliance Industries’ statement that it welcomes competition in satellite communications, provided all players follow Indian laws and policies.“We have worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for 5+ years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic safely and securely - and all with the requisite government approvals. Starlink is ready to connect India with high-speed internet,” the company said in a post on X.The response after Reliance Industries pushed back against Elon Musk’s allegations that certain business groups were blocking Starlink’s entry into India.Reliance said it welcomed competition and that every player, including Jio, must comply with the country’s laws and policies. It also noted that Jio’s own satellite services were awaiting clearances."In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record.Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances," Reliance had said.Musk had accused “certain oligarchs” of blocking Starlink’s entry into India before naming Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani in a series of posts.The government has also rejected Musk’s claims. Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said satellite spectrum would be assigned once the government finalised the revenue-sharing framework and companies met security requirements.Starlink, Reliance Jio and Eutelsat OneWeb have received licences to provide satellite communication services in India. The services are expected to extend internet connectivity to remote areas where laying conventional broadband infrastructure is difficult. articles.title: IDBI Bank disinvestment: Govt clarifies shareholding concerns, says 2003 law does not restrict stake dilution
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The finance ministry on Saturday clarified that the government’s power to dilute its stake in IDBI Bank was not restricted by the IDBI (Repeal)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The finance ministry on Saturday clarified that the government’s power to dilute its stake in IDBI Bank was not restricted by the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003. The statement comes amid media reports on the 2003 legislative developments concerning the government’s shareholding in the bank.The ministry said that an amendment seeking to restrict the dilution of the government’s stake was moved during the Union Budget 2003 discussions and parliamentary debate on the Act, but was rejected and did not become part of the enacted legislation.The ministry cited the Delhi High Court’s December 17, 2018, judgment in All India IDBI Officers’ Association vs. Union of India and Others, which dismissed a petition challenging the government’s decision to dilute its shareholding.In paragraph 41, the court held, “This Court is of the view that the statements made before the House almost 15 years earlier, in a debate relating to a legislative activity, would not preclude the Central Government from diluting its stake in IDBI Ltd. Indisputably, the legislation enacted by the Parliament after the debate did not contain the amendment that was sought to be introduced. The statements made before the House cannot substitute or override the statue so enacted by the Parliament.”Paragraph 42 stated, “There is no ambiguity in the language of the IDBI Repeal Act, 2003 and there is no scope to read any provision into the said enactment which proscribes the Government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Ltd.”The government said the ruling clarified that the doctrine of promissory estoppel could not be invoked to prevent it from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Bank.“The aforesaid judgment is significant as it specifically addresses the doctrine of promissory estoppel, which was relied upon in challenging the Government’s decision to dilute its shareholding. The doctrine could not be invoked to prevent the Government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Ltd,” the official statement said.Budget speeches on IDBI disinvestmentThe ministry also cited Budget announcements tracing the government’s disinvestment policy. In his 2016–17 Budget speech, then finance minister Arun Jaitley said, “Our Public Sector Banks will have to be strong and competitive. The Bank Board Bureau will be operationalised during 2016-17 and a roadmap for consolidation of Public Sector Banks will be spelt out.The process of transformation of IDBI Bank has already started. Government will take it forward and also consider the option of reducing its stake to below 50%.”In the 2021–22 Budget, then finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman listed IDBI Bank among transactions targeted for completion during the year.She said, “In spite of COVID-19, we have kept working towards strategic disinvestment. A number of transactions namely BPCL, Air India, Shipping Corporation of India, Container Corporation of India, IDBI Bank, BEML, Pawan Hans, Neelachal Ispat Nigam limited among others would be completed in 2021-22. Other than IDBI Bank, we propose to take up the privatization of two Public Sector Banks and one General Insurance company in the year 2021-22. This would require legislative amendments and I propose to introduce the amendments in this Session itself.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: How the US-Iran war upended two critical global trade routes
articles.summary: The war between the United States and Iran has upended the global oil market by severely disrupting the flow of oil through two critical waterways: the Strait of Hormuz and, in recent weeks, the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.
articles.body: The war between the United States and Iran has upended the global oil market by severely disrupting the flow of oil through two critical waterways: the Strait of Hormuz and, in recent weeks, the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Iran is now stepping up attacks on tankers transiting Hormuz and the Persian Gulf, curtailing the volume of oil exiting the region and keeping global crude prices north of $100 a barrel. There have been 12 reported attacks on vessels in or near Hormuz in the past week, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, which monitors maritime security in the region. And, earlier this week, two cargo ships sank after attacks by unknown projectiles in separate incidents. Analysts say intensifying attacks by Iran are in response to the large quantities of oil that have managed to exit Hormuz in recent weeks. The US military has led an effective operation to ferry oil across the strait by assisting “dark” transits – tankers sailing with their transponders turned off and shuttling oil to ships waiting in the Gulf of Oman. Meanwhile, Iran continues to struggle to sail its own tankers through the waterway because of a US naval blockade. The conflict, now in its eighth month, has also widened to include fighting between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen. The Houthis have targeted Saudi oil tankers transiting the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and, in recent days, launched deadly strikes on Riyadh’s main international airport. The crisis will have long-term ramifications on the global oil market, say analysts. Oil-importing countries increasingly understand they must “structurally reduce their oil consumption” to become less vulnerable to external shocks, Georg Zachmann, a senior fellow at think tank Bruegel, told CNN. That, alongside other measures, could help “shield (them) from this increasingly uncertain world,” he said. The Bab al-Mandeb Strait became more strategically important after the war disrupted the neighboring Strait of Hormuz. At its peak, around 4.5 million barrels of crude per day were exported from the Saudi Red Sea port of Yanbu, with the bulk – about 3 million barrels per day – exiting via Bab al-Mandeb, according to Richard Bronze, co-founder of Energy Aspects. But those flows “collapsed” after the Houthi threat started escalating this summer, he said. Johannes Rauball, senior crude analyst at Kpler, said that if the Houthis begin threatening ships from all countries, “This would really create another blow for crude markets. It would really push prices higher again, really tighten balances.” But after an attack last month by drones from inside Iraq on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline – which pumps crude toward the country’s Red Sea ports – Riyadh pivoted quickly, stepping up crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz via the US military-assisted shuttle operation. US President Donald Trump said Iran was probably behind the September attack, with Iran-backed militia groups known to operate inside Iraq. Iran’s foreign ministry has “categorically denied” the accusation. The East-West pipeline is now back online, according to several reports. Asian countries — the biggest buyers of Saudi oil — have borne the brunt of the crisis during the war, but they have adapted by cutting consumption. China has also greatly reduced its imports by tapping into its strategic reserves. The crisis has also pushed some Middle Eastern countries to explore new export routes through yet-to-be-built pipelines. “The longer this conflict drags on, the less leverage Iran actually has, because other countries are able to create bypass routes,” Rauball, at Kpler, said.

articles.title: Hasta 80.000 euros al año por limpiar ventanas en rascacielos a cientos de metros de altura: "Escucho mucha música"
articles.standfirst: "Empecé como escalador e intenté dedicarme a eso para ganarme la vida", explica
articles.summary: "Empecé como escalador e intenté dedicarme a eso para ganarme la vida", explica
articles.body: Los rascacielos son estructuras imponentes que, como cualquier edificio, requieren mantenimiento y limpieza. Eso implica las numerosas ventanas de sus fachadas. Un limpiacristales de Vancouver (Canadá) relató qué se siente al estar colgado en las alturas y firmando un trabajo claramente de riesgo. "Es bastante divertido. Estoy conmigo mismo y escucho un montón de música, principalmente country", se sinceró en el canal de TikTok Daniella_atk. Este joven se inició como escalador en roca, su gran pasión, y pretendía enfocar su carrera profesional hacia esa dirección. De todos modos, no tuvo éxito. "Empecé como escalador e intenté dedicarme a eso para ganarme la vida. Realmente no vale mucho la pena serlo, así que limpiar rascacielos es lo siguiente mejor", comentó con humor durante la entrevista. "Intento estar a salvo porque es un trabajo peligroso. Una vez me picó un pájaro", bromeó. La música y la soledad en las alturas le motivan, aunque también el sueldo. Ante la cámara del canal de TikTok, no tiene reparos en detallar sus condiciones laborales. "Nos pagan en función del trabajo que hagamos. Normalmente ganamos alrededor de unos 60 dólares (canadienses) la hora", explicó. Saquemos la calculadora: a 60 dólares canadienses la hora, con el cambio monetario actual a euros, este joven limpiador de ventanas de rascacielos podría ingresar unos 80.000 euros al año con una jornada de ocho horas, cinco días a la semana. Muchos de los usuarios de la publicación se han mostrado sorprendidos por esta cantidad. "¿60 dólares la hora? Es momento de cambiar de profesión. Ya no tengo miedo a las alturas", puede leerse en los comentarios de la red social. Por otra parte, buscando en España trabajos relativamente comparables, de limpiacristales en altura, asumiendo que un rascacielos es un escenario distinto, encontramos que las ofertas plantean sueldos que no superan los 24.000 euros brutos anuales.
